providers.name: BLM Island Bar Lower Salmon public put-in access anchor
providers.method: BLM publishes the Island Bar site coordinate and identifies this undeveloped Lower Salmon recreation site as a frequent put-in with easy river access. Keep the point as a recreation-site/access anchor; it does not identify a surveyed shoreline landing or ramp toe. Verify current site and beach conditions.

controls.name: Island Bar Recreation Site
controls.coordinateText: Stored coordinate matches the BLM-published site coordinate within one foot; BLM describes easy river access but does not designate an exact wetted-edge point.

providers.name: Burwell Riverside Park North Loup water-trail start access anchor
providers.method: Burwell’s municipal plan places Riverside Park on the west bank of the North Loup near North 8th Street. Nebraska Game and Parks’ current water-trails page links its North Loup trip planner, which names Riverside Park as the trail start. The stored point is retained as a park/access-area anchor; neither source publishes a surveyed launch coordinate.

controls.name: Burwell Riverside Park
controls.coordinateText: Existing park-side route pin retained; official sources establish the public trail start and west-bank park location, not a specific wet-edge coordinate.

providers.name: Colerain Obergiesing Soccer Complex at Dravo Park canoe-ramp access anchor
providers.method: Colerain Township identifies the named facility as one of its two Great Miami River canoe ramps and lists parking and dawn-to-dusk public hours. Retain the existing facility-area point; the township publishes no exact ramp-toe coordinate.

controls.name: Obergiesing Soccer Complex at Dravo Park canoe-ramp access
controls.coordinateText: Existing park/facility pin for the township-confirmed public canoe-ramp site; not a surveyed ramp toe.

providers.name: Michigan DNR Charles Besemer Muskegon River Park boat access at Croton Dam
providers.method: Michigan DNR publishes this exact coordinate for Charles Besemer Muskegon River Park boat access at Croton Dam and describes the steep paved launch, trailer parking and below-dam access context. The coordinate is the DNR access-site point; retain it and do not shift it to another nearby pin.

controls.name: Charles Besemer Muskegon River Park boat access at Croton Dam
aliases: Croton Dam Tailwater Park public boat launch
controls.coordinateText: Exact Michigan DNR published coordinate for the named below-dam boat access; public route starts below the dam.

providers.name: Willamette Riverkeeper Norwood Island paddle-in campsite access anchor
providers.method: Willamette Water Trail publishes the stored site coordinate, RM 148.5, Riverkeeper management, and a campsite on the mainstem side toward the downstream end of the island. Keep this as an island/campsite anchor; paddlers must scout the actual landing and current channel. The back-channel bridge is washed out.

controls.name: Norwood Island paddle-in campsite
controls.coordinateText: Water-trail operator site coordinate for the managed island/campsite; landing point varies with channel and bank conditions.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Spring Hill Sauk River public water access feature
providers.method: Minnesota public-water-access GIS feature OBJECTID 2500 / WAS00338 returns WGS84 x=-94.775652824582878, y=45.529866726150793, names Stearns County as administrator and identifies the Sauk River RM56.1 public access. DNR Map 2 lists Spring Hill carry-in sites at RM56.2 on the left bank and RM56.1 on the right bank; the stored route endpoint is standardized to this named GIS access feature and its mapped access-area coordinate, not claimed as a surveyed launch toe.
